messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] pcount (N-mixture model) to assess species richness
parts:
Dear Manuel,

in the AHM1 book (chapter 11) we give such an example, but discuss in which way this is supoptimal: this approach accounts a little bit for detection probability, but assumes that all species occurring at a site during a particular survey occasion have the same p. This assumption may be OK for the traditional application of the model to populations of the same species, but it is likely to be very problematic when an "individual" is equal to a species, because there is always tremendous variation in p among species. This is going to bias your estimates of species richness.

Better to use some of the recent advances for multi-species occupancy models by Chris Sutherland and Simone Tenan. They show how you can directly model species richness as a function of covariates. But you have to go down the BUGS road.
 
Best regards  --- Marc
